content: Metabolife is an American company that specializes in the production of dietary supplements. Its most popular product, Metabolife 356, was an ephedra-based supplement that once generated over $1 billion in annual sales. However, Metabolife 356 and other supplements containing ephedra were associated with thousands of severe adverse events, including fatalities. This led the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to ban dietary supplements containing ephedra in 2004, deeming them unsafe. Michael Ellis, the founder of Metabolife, was charged with eight counts of making false statements to the FDA in an attempt to obstruct regulatory oversight of ephedra. Additionally, Metabolife was investigated by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and the Department of Justice (DOJ) for income tax evasion. The company ultimately pled guilty to filing fraudulent tax returns and was ordered to pay a criminal fine of $600,000. William Bradley, the owner of Metabolife, also pled guilty to evading millions of dollars in taxes. He was sentenced to six months in federal prison and two years of probation. Facing declining sales and over $1 billion in personal injury lawsuits related to Metabolife 356, the company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2005. To address its debts and settle outstanding personal injury claims, Metabolife liquidated its assets, including a significant collection of artwork, in late 2006.
